name: Acrokeratosis Verruciformis of Hopf

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Acrokeratosis Verruciformis of Hopf

criteria.description: Presence of multiple flat-topped, wart-like papules predominantly on the dorsal aspects of hands and feet
Histopathological findings showing hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, and papillomatosis resembling verruca plana
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of mutations in the ATP2A2 gene (overlap with Darier disease gene) in some cases

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesions plus confirmatory histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may aid diagnosis but is not mandatory; differentiation from Darier disease is essential.

searchTerms: tiny hardened patches on palms and soles
punctate keratoderma on hands and feet

other: Histopathology showing hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, papillomatosis without dyskeratosis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of greasy, crusted keratotic papules
Histopathology showing dyskeratosis and corps ronds
More widespread involvement including seborrheic areas
Risk of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma

redFlags: Rapid progression or ulceration of lesions
Development of malignant transformation in longstanding lesions
references: Bolognia JL, Schaffer JV, Cerroni L. Dermatology. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2018.
